result: No open production correctness or safety findings within the reviewed scope. One documentation qualification was reported and is now resolved in the current allocator-usage.md.
method: Read-only production call-path review, allocation-site/push/clone/pointer scans, and local safety-proof review. No builds, tests, benchmarks, repository edits, or commits were performed for this audit.

checks.conclusion: compress_in, compress_with_dictionary_in, decompress_in, decompress_with_options_in, decompress_with_dictionary_in, dictionary parsing and raw/formatted training preserve the original allocator in the returned byte owner. Independent scratch owners retain fresh clones; no raw-parts transfers or buffer allocator substitutions were found.

Runtime codec payload creation/growth is preceded by try_reserve or try_reserve_exact. Capacity-proven individual pushes, slice copy/fill and allocation-free sort_unstable operations replace infallible allocation-capable bulk insertion. Remaining reserve/extend search hits are private checked wrappers; remaining Vec::new constructors are explicit Global specializations or test-only support.

FSE channel commit swaps whole owners; setup failures drop partial local arrays/tables. Huffman description validation borrows its allocator only within a scope that ends before description movement. Streaming errors retain the poison-until-reset contract and claimed/unclaimed prefix distinction.

Private views borrow initialized slices and plain repeated/scalar records. Shared handles clone ownership without cloning payload allocators; custom dictionary storage types remain independent of workspace A. No references into adjacent context fields persist.

Reviewed all twelve gated families. Runtime bounds or fixed-width hash bounds remain valid for allocator-generic Vec owners and borrowed table views. Raw writes remain within fallibly reserved capacity and initialize bytes before length publication; pointer/reference lifetimes do not outlive their retained owner. No allocator-equivalence, Global-specific layout, or alignment assumption was found.

Default library builds forbid unsafe_code when no backend flags are enabled. Production code uses core/alloc, while entropy-output/oracles/filesystem/process helpers remain test-only. Global shared ownership uses Arc on pointer-atomic targets and Rc otherwise, with the outer allocation explicitly outside custom payload control.

Public lifetime, custom Clone, exact-owner, borrowed allocator and retained-capacity claims agree with the reviewed implementation. The blanket fallibility sentence was narrowed to payload requests and now explicitly names the standard infallible Global into_shared allocation.

resolved_findings.issue: Original blanket codec-owned allocation-failure statement omitted into_shared infallibility qualification.
resolved_findings.resolution: Coordinator changed the text to codec payload growth and explicitly documented standard infallible Global Arc/Rc outer storage; verified by readback.

limitations: This is a source review, not a new dynamic validation campaign or a proof against every conforming/malicious allocator implementation.

One-shot encoder production was reviewed after its owning agent confirmed the body frozen; that agent was still adding tests and running its final matrix. Whole-file hashes include the observed test contents and may change through subsequent test-only edits.
Other agents may update documentation, tests, or commit source already reviewed. These hashes describe this readback checkpoint; future production changes require review.
Only the installed dated compiler and previously recorded target evidence are supported; this audit does not add a Rust 1.100, stable compiler, 32-bit, non-atomic, or cross-platform execution claim.

Allocator callbacks and Clone retain their ordinary contract, allocation and panic behavior. Global Arc/Rc outer storage, caller buffers, test ledgers, and external C oracle storage are explicit exclusions.
